title: Hospital Account (Encounter Billing): Figuring the Non-Covered Discount
content:
**Clause.** On a Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) account, the non-covered amount is the total of the account's non-covered-service liability postings; an account with none has a non-covered amount of 0.00 and receives no non-covered discount. The non-covered discount is the patient class's uninsured discount percent (from the uninsured discount schedule) of the non-covered amount, rounded half-up to the cent.

**Combination.** Percentage points are combined with that figure this way: every allowance stated in percentage points is added to the non-covered discount percent, the combined percent is applied once to the non-covered amount and the product is rounded half-up to the cent, and the resulting non-covered discount never exceeds the non-covered amount.

## Quantities

| Quantity | What it is |
|---|---|
| Non-covered amount | total of all non-covered-service liability postings on the account |
| Non-covered discount percent | the patient class's uninsured discount percent, with any percentage points added to it |
| Non-covered discount | that percent of the non-covered amount, applied once, rounded half-up to the cent, at most the non-covered amount |

## Worked figure (hypothetical inputs)

An account carries two non-covered-service liability postings of 600.00 and 400.00, so its non-covered amount is 1000.00. On a patient class whose uninsured discount percent were 40, the non-covered discount is 40 percent of 1000.00, that is 400.00.

With a hypothetical 3.5 percentage points added, the combined percent is 43.5, applied once to 1000.00: 435.00.

*Rounding (hypothetical).* A non-covered amount of 333.33 at 40 percent gives 133.332, rounded half-up to 133.33.
